# gitmoap_group_wiki_page (Data Source)

Read one wiki page. Answers the page's content, its table of contents and the wiki's head commit, which you send back as `expected_head_sha` when you save an edit. A page that has moved is still found at its old address, and the response then names the address you asked for so you can update the link. The table of contents can be empty for a page written moments ago, until it has been indexed. Anyone who can see the group may read its wiki; on a public group that includes callers who are not signed in.

The token needs `wiki:read`.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `group_id` (String) Group ID
- `path` (String) URL-encoded wiki page path

### Read-Only

- `commit` (Attributes) One commit in a page's history. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--commit))
- `content` (String) The markup, read from git at the wiki's head.
- `created_at` (String)
- `created_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--created_by))
- `doc_id` (String) Stable identity. **Unchanged by a rename**, which is what lets every backlink survive one.
- `format` (String) The markup a page is written in, decided by its file extension.
- `head_sha` (String)
- `redirected_from` (String)
- `title` (String)
- `toc` (Attributes List) From `spec_blocks`. Empty until the projection has caught up, which is a different thing
from the page having no headings and is why the page itself is never sourced from there. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--toc))
- `updated_at` (String)
- `wiki_id` (String)
- `wiki_page_id` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--commit"></a>
### Nested Schema for `commit`

Read-Only:

- `author` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--commit--author))
- `author_name` (String)
- `committed_at` (String)
- `message` (String)
- `sha` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--commit--author"></a>
### Nested Schema for `commit.author`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor and empty on a redacted one.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor.
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.

<a id="nestedatt--toc"></a>
### Nested Schema for `toc`

Read-Only:

- `anchor` (String) The GitHub-compatible slug, which is what a link into the page uses.
- `heading` (String)
- `level` (Number)
- `ordinal` (Number)
- `parent_ordinal` (Number) The enclosing heading's ordinal, so a client can rebuild the tree without a second read.
